title: bun test: Snapshot Engine, Native Mock Hoisting, and Jest Compatibility

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Jest and Vitest are like heavy test trucks that take seconds just to warm up and load their tools. `bun test` is built directly into Bun in native code: it runs thousands of tests, mocks functions, and checks snapshots in milliseconds before Jest even finishes starting up.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `bun test` is Bun's built-in, Jest-compatible test runner. Run tests with `bun test`. It imports standard `describe`, `it`, `test`, `expect`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`, and `mock` from `bun:test`. It natively supports TypeScript and JSX out of the box with zero configuration files (`babel.config.js` or `tsconfig.json` test loaders are not required).
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `bun test` achieves extreme test velocity by avoiding transpilation overhead. Jest and Vitest must spin up worker processes in Node, initialize Babel/esbuild transforms, and serialize results across IPC. `bun test` runs test files directly inside JavaScriptCore native isolates, leveraging SIMD snapshot string comparisons and native module mock hoisting via `mock.module()`.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: The `bun:test` runner is implemented in Zig and C++. When `bun test` executes, it discovers matching test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.tsx`), batches them across CPU cores, compiles them with the native Zig transpiler, and evaluates them inside JSC. `expect().toMatchSnapshot()` reads and writes to `__snapshots__/*.snap` using native fast file I/O, and `mock.module()` directly overrides entries in the module map.

interviewGotchas.question: How does module mocking work in `bun:test` via `mock.module`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of dependency mocking in Bun.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Use `mock.module('module-name', () => { return { myExport: () => 'mocked' }; })`. `mock.module` intercepts the module resolution map inside the JavaScriptCore runtime. Any subsequent import of `'module-name'` throughout the test suite will receive the mocked exports.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: `mock.module` hoists automatically, but to restore original module implementations, call `mock.restore()` or `mock.module()` with the original factory.

interviewGotchas.question: Can `bun test` run tests in a simulated browser DOM environment (like jsdom)?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of DOM testing setups in Bun.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Yes. You can install `happy-dom` or `jsdom` and configure Bun to use it by creating a preload script: `bun test --preload ./setup-dom.ts` where `setup-dom.ts` attaches `window`, `document`, and DOM globals to `globalThis`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Bun does not ship with built-in DOM elements in the runtime core; DOM globals must be provided via `happy-dom` or `jsdom` for React/Vue component tests.
